exhibits.title: Exhibit A — Study Crime Scene Sketch (9:02 PM)
exhibits.html:
• Door & Window: Heavy oak double-door bolted from the inside; cliff window latched inside.
  • The Body: Lord Arthur Vance slumped across his desk blotter. First reached and rolled over by Vivienne Sterling at 9:01 PM.
  • Initial Statement (9:01 PM): As guests rushed in, Vivienne Sterling loudly claimed to see Arthur's "chalk-pale lips" and smell "bitter almonds from the spilled wine."
  • On the Desk: Unsigned New Will; a crystal wine glass; a single poured porcelain cup of chamomile tea (barely lukewarm by 9:02 PM); a broken pocket watch.
  • On the Floor: Shattered glass beside a heavy 5-lb brass counterweight in a pool of spilled liquid.

exhibits.title: Exhibit B — Arthur's Shattered Pocket Watch
exhibits.html:
• Make: Custom Vance Precision Gold Chronometer ("A.V. — Time Never Lies").
  • Condition: Crystal cracked; internal gears jammed from hitting the desk corner.
  • Frozen Time: 8:48 PM (12 minutes before the 9:00 PM blackout).
  • Witness Note: Vivienne Sterling snapped the gold lid shut at 9:01 PM, claiming Arthur's watch "always ran twelve minutes slow."

prologue.label: PROLOGUE — 9:00 PM
prologue.sub: Read aloud (or click Read Aloud) to set the scene at Ravenshollow Manor.
prologue.html:
Welcome to Ravenshollow Manor. Outside, a violent November nor'easter has washed out the wooden bridge to the mainland, and the telephone lines are dead. You are guests of billionaire clockmaker Lord Arthur Vance (72).

At 8:45 PM, Arthur retired alone to his second-floor Study to fetch his New Will, bolting the heavy oak door from the inside. At 8:55 PM, guests in the Grand Hall heard Arthur shouting from upstairs: "You've gone too far! I'm calling the police as soon as the lines are back!"

At 9:00 PM sharp, as the Grand Astronomical Clock struck nine, the backup generator died—plunging the manor into darkness for 15 seconds. A sharp crack and heavy thud echoed from the Study. When the lights returned at 9:01 PM, you broke down the bolted door—and found Arthur Vance dead at his desk.

Vivienne Sterling (#17)

revealHtml:
The Truth Behind the Last Chime (RV-2255)

The Killer: Vivienne Sterling (#17)
The Accomplice (Shadow Team): Father Silas Ward (#13)
The Inspector: Clara Sterling (#2)

Arthur Vance did not die at 9:00 PM. He died at 8:48 PM—alone behind a bolted door—from concentrated Aconite hidden in the gilded tin of French anise mints handed to him by Vivienne Sterling (#17) at 8:42 PM. At 9:01 PM, Vivienne Sterling rushed to the desk first, pocketing the gilded tin of French anise mints and later ditching a botanical-smudged handkerchief down the upstairs laundry chute.

Victor Vance (#5) spiked the red wine with harmless sleeping powder, which Arthur never touched. The 8:55 PM argument was a pre-recorded brass wax cylinder played by the Chronos Automaton, and the 9:00 PM crash was the counterweight smashing the water carafe while blackmailed accomplice Father Silas Ward (#13) cut the generator breaker for 15 seconds.

The 4-Pillar Proof: (1) Arthur's pocket watch froze at 8:48 PM and his Horologist Journal proves it never lost a second; (2) The wine was untouched and Arthur died of odorless Aconite from the gilded tin of French anise mints; (3) Vivienne Sterling slipped up in Act I by claiming to see Arthur's pale lips (Arthur was face-down!) and smell bitter almonds from spilled wine (it was odorless water!); (4) Exhibit C flagged both "S.W." and "V.S.", but Exhibit E clears Father Silas Ward (no 2008 access) and ties Vivienne Sterling directly to 2008 Evidence Tampering — Altered Deposition — Legal Clerk, Sterling & Vance (2008)!
